fact: Connecting Africa reports that the April 2025 Sotel-Airtel MoU for the N'Djamena-Mbere fibre route from Chad to the Cameroon border was suspended by Chad's ARCEP, and that Chad's government urged the operators to revise it before work can start; no agreement is in force and works have not begun.

The AfDB communique says the Central African Republic's national fibre backbone, 935 km of terrestrial and under-river fibre installed and made operational, was inaugurated on 6 February 2023 and interconnects the CAR, Cameroon (via Gamboula) and Congo, as a component of the Central African Backbone project.
system: Dorsale à fibre optique d'Afrique centrale (Central African Backbone - CAB)

fact: SPIN (Gabon) reports that the partners signed a memorandum of understanding and a confidentiality agreement on CAB-CORRIDOR, a terrestrial interconnection between Cameroon, Gabon and the Republic of Congo over the Central African Backbone, with implementation modalities due in October 2026; signing dates are not given, so the document's publication date is used.

Cameroon and Chad's ministers concluded a four-day technical mission on 2025-05-16 that finalised, among other items, the imminent completion of the Nana-Mbere fibre optic section within fourteen days, with an action plan of targets through July 2025.
